findings.finding: The new test calls `late._screenshot_check_issue(...)` but the diff adds no import of `late` into this test module; the visible context shows only `validate_phase(...)` used by the existing tests. If the module's existing imports don't already bind `late`, this test raises `NameError` at collection/run time — and if they do, the finding is void, but the diff gives no evidence either way.
findings.suggestion: Verify the module imports the `phase_validators_late` module (e.g. `from plugins.shipwright_run.scripts.lib import phase_validators_late as late`); add the import explicitly if missing.

findings.finding: The `carries()` predicate hardcodes `kit_css[200:600].strip() in html` and `class="topnav` — it validates an arbitrary byte-slice of the shipped CSS, not the documented definition (kit CSS inline, `:root` token block, kit component classes, no colour/font/size literal). Any edit to `kit.css` lines 200–600 (whitespace-only edits included) silently breaks or voids the test, and the negative cases don't exercise the definition's real clauses (e.g. a screen pasting kit CSS but with its own hex literals would count as "carrying the kit" here).
findings.suggestion: Assert on stable markers (e.g. the first rule selector and a distinctive component class) rather than a byte slice, and add a negative case for "kit CSS inline but own colour literals" if the intent is to pin the definition.

findings.finding: The "composed screen passes the standalone gate" test uses the shipped kit example itself as the package mockup, so the applied screen is a byte-copy of an already-standalone page. It cannot fail unless `apply-brief-package.py` itself breaks; it does not exercise any composition behaviour. Weak, though the architecture decision explicitly scoped tests to "checking instructions, not agent output", so this is a pinning test at best.
findings.suggestion: Either accept it as a regression pin with a comment saying so, or drop the misleading name.

findings.finding: The "A crash mid-compose..." paragraph sits between numbered steps 5 and 6 with no blank-line separation, so in rendered markdown step 6 ("Run `check-design-gates.py --gate all`") detaches from the list and the crash note reads as part of step 5's "compose it and re-run the gates" (which itself is confusing: gates run in step 6, so "re-run the gates" from step 5 has no defined meaning yet).
findings.suggestion: Move the crash note to the Limits section (or after step 6) and reword step 5's recovery as "compose it before continuing to step 6".

findings.finding: The routing says a red `standalone`/`chrome` gate is a package defect only when "caused by package content rather than by a screen you composed" — but the applied screen is the package content until it's composed, so an agent hitting a red `standalone` gate before/during composition (e.g. a mockup with relative assets, which is the cited package defect) can't disambiguate: composing the screen would fix the relative-asset problem, yet upload-mode.md still lists "a mockup with relative assets" as package CONTENT → STOP. The two rules now conflict for that exact case.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly that relative-asset mockups remain a package STOP even though composition could technically inline them (or say composition must not repair package defects by fetching/inlining external assets).

findings.finding: The updated assertions pin exact phrasing ("on the COMPOSED screens (compose first)"), which is fine, but note the SKILL.md assertion `"APPLIED screens" not in skill` in `test_brief_compose_prose.py` will fail if any other section of SKILL.md legitimately retains "APPLIED screens" wording in future — a broad whole-file negative assertion on a 300-line file is fragile. Low risk today.
findings.suggestion: Scope the negative assertion to the brief-package section if it grows.

findings.finding: The new “carries the kit” definition treats any screen with its own colour, font, or size literal as an uncomposed mockup and instructs the agent to rewrite it. A previously composed screen with such an adjustment from the review loop will therefore lose approved edits on resume, contradicting the requirement that review-loop edits survive.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish incomplete initial composition from subsequent review edits. Preserve previously composed screens on resume even when review feedback introduced custom styling.

findings.finding: Every Brief screen must now satisfy the kit composition rules, while legacy chat-first packages with other profiles still require Layout D. The diff explicitly states that Layout D is not part of the kit, yet the composition self-check requires every screen to use kit components. These supported legacy packages receive incompatible instructions, potentially replacing their required layout or repeatedly failing the self-check.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly exempt supported legacy chat-first screens from the universal kit composition requirement, or define a compatible kit-based Layout D and its self-check criteria.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The prose-only approach matches the architecture decision, but its resume and legacy-package instructions need correction before shipping.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
